David and Solomon judged a case of sheep overrunning a field, with Solomon given understanding; the mountains and birds glorified Allah with David, who was taught to make armor.
Allah subjected the wind to Solomon, blowing by his command to the blessed land, and some devils dived and worked for him under Allah's guard.
Job called to his Lord in adversity, and Allah removed it and restored his family with as many more, as a mercy and a reminder for worshippers.
Ishmael, Idrees and Dhul-Kifl were all patient, admitted into Allah's mercy and counted among the righteous.
The man of the fish left in anger, then called from the darknesses that there is no deity but Allah and he had done wrong; Allah answered and saved him.
Zechariah asked not to be left without an heir; Allah answered, gave him John and amended his wife; they hastened to good deeds and supplicated in hope and fear.
The woman who guarded her chastity was breathed into through Allah's angel, and she and her son were made a sign for the worlds.
Your religion is one religion and Allah is your Lord, so worship Him; yet they divided their affair among themselves, and all will return to Him.
Whoever does righteous deeds as a believer will not have his effort denied, for Allah records it.
The people of a destroyed city will not return until Gog and Magog are let loose from every height and the true promise nears, when the disbelievers stare in horror.
Disbelievers and what they worship besides Allah will be fuel for Hell, while those promised the best are far from it, untroubled by the greatest terror and welcomed by angels.
On that Day Allah will fold the heaven like a scroll of records and repeat creation as He began it, a promise binding on Him.
Allah wrote in the Psalms, after the earlier mention, that His righteous servants will inherit the land, and this Quran is a notification for worshipping people.
The Prophet, sent as a mercy to the worlds, announces your god is one God, does not know when the promise comes, and asks his Lord to judge in truth.
Mankind is told to fear their Lord, for the convulsion of the Hour is terrible: nursing mothers will be distracted, pregnant women will miscarry, and people will seem intoxicated.
Some dispute about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil, and whoever turns to a devil is misguided by him and led to the punishment of the Blaze.
Doubters of the Resurrection are reminded of their creation from dust in stages and barren earth revived by rain; Allah revives the dead and will raise those in graves.
Some dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance or scripture, twisting away in arrogance to mislead; they face disgrace in this world and the Burning Fire on the Day of Resurrection.
Some worship Allah on an edge, content when good touches them but turning away when trial strikes, and so lose both this world and the Hereafter.
Invoking instead of Allah what neither harms nor benefits is extreme error, and what is invoked has harm closer than its benefit, a wretched protector and associate.
Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow, for Allah does what He intends.
Whoever thinks Allah will not support the Prophet in this world and the Hereafter is told to stretch a rope to the ceiling and see if that removes his rage.
Allah has sent the Quran down as verses of clear evidence, and Allah guides whom He intends.
Allah will judge on the Day of Resurrection between the believers, Jews, Sabeans, Christians, Magians and those who associate others with Him, for He witnesses all things.
All in the heavens and earth prostrate to Allah, with the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, creatures and many people, while punishment is justified upon many others.
Two adversaries dispute over their Lord, a verse revealed about the duel at Badr: disbelievers get garments of fire, scalding water and iron maces, believers wear gold, pearl and silk.
Those who disbelieve and bar people from Allah's way and from al-Masjid al-Haram, equal for resident and visitor, will taste painful punishment, as will anyone intending wrongdoing there.
Abraham is given the site of the House to purify it and proclaim the Hajj; pilgrims come, mention Allah over sacrificial animals, feed the poor and circle the House.
Honoring Allah's sacred ordinances is best; livestock is permitted except what is recited, idols and false statements must be avoided, and associating with Allah is like falling from the sky.
Honoring Allah's symbols comes from piety; every religion has a rite of sacrifice, camels and cattle are offered in Allah's name, eaten and shared, and only piety reaches Allah.
Allah defends those who believe and does not like anyone treacherous and ungrateful.
In the first permission to fight, Muslims wronged and driven from Makkah for saying their Lord is Allah may fight; given authority, they establish prayer, give zakah and enjoin right.
Before the Prophet, the peoples of Noah, 'Aad, Thamud, Abraham, Lot and Madyan denied, as Moses was denied; Allah let them enjoy, then seized them, leaving cities in ruin.
They urge the Prophet to hasten the punishment, but Allah never fails His promise, a day with Him is like a thousand years, and He seized many cities after respite.
The Prophet is only a clear warner: believers who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision, while those who strive against Allah's verses are companions of Hellfire.
Satan threw something into the speech of every messenger or prophet, but Allah abolishes it and makes His verses precise, a trial for diseased hearts while the knowledgeable believe.
Disbelievers stay in doubt until the Hour comes suddenly; that Day all sovereignty is Allah's, believers enter the Gardens of Pleasure and deniers of His signs face humiliating punishment.
Those who emigrated for Allah's cause and then were killed or died will receive a good provision from Allah and an entrance that pleases them.
Whoever responds to harm with its equivalent and is then wronged again will be aided by Allah, who is Pardoning and Forgiving.
Allah merges night and day, sends rain that greens the earth, owns all, subjects the earth and ships to people, holds up the sky, and gives life and death.
